## Findings

- **Main implementation:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ) — target locking, player movement, boss AI, twin models, attacks, and procedural animation are implemented here.
- **HUD controls:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html ) — lines 41 and 61 label **Q** as “auto-lock nearest enemy” / release.
- **Built copy:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/dist/game.js`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/dist/game.js ) — contains the corresponding game implementation.

### Target lock and movement

- `game.js` lines **5152, 5265–5312**: Q toggles lock-on. Target selection considers visible active bosses or living duo twins, plus non-dying skeletons, and chooses the nearest. The lock can be released with Q.
- Lines **6182–6215** and **7841–7916**: lock-on turns the player toward the target, changes movement to strafe relative to the facing direction, and affects camera behavior.
- Lines **4825–4898**: duo AI movement and attack-state updates. Vesper maintains a longer distance (about 9 units); Morrow approaches closer (about 3.5). Twins keep space from each other and are constrained to the arena.

### Vesper and Morrow

- Lines **3324–3378**: both are procedural `buildKnight` models, with no external model or animation assets indicated. Vesper has pale frost-blue armor, a mask, halo, and candle details; Morrow has darker armor, a bell, and a greatsword.
- Lines **4679–4701**: twin and duo state, health, attack ownership, and requiem/revival tracking.
- Lines **4750–4824**: attack choice and resolution. Vesper uses frostbolt, frostfall, and frostwave attacks; Morrow uses cleave, slam, and charge. The shared `attackOwner` state gates attacks so only one twin attacks at a time.
- Lines **5037–5059**: procedural posing uses `poseKnight` plus custom arm, halo, candle, bell, and sword-glow motion. A fallen twin can return through the requiem/revival logic in the duo state and update sections.

### Other useful references

- Lines **2391 onward**: shared procedural knight model builder.
- Lines **4470–4475**: duo boss identity and description.
- Lines **5255–5263**: lock-relative movement direction and attack-arc helpers.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
BUILD_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/dist"

if [[ ! "$PORT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( PORT < 1 || PORT > 65535 )); then
  echo "PORT must be an integer from 1 to 65535 (got: $PORT)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?OPENCODE_WEB_DIR must point to the worker metadata directory}"

if [[ -f package.json ]]; then
  /usr/bin/time -p npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
fi

/usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
/usr/bin/time -p cp index.html game.js style.css "$BUILD_DIR/"
/usr/bin/time -p test -s "$BUILD_DIR/index.html"
/usr/bin/time -p test -s "$BUILD_DIR/game.js"
/usr/bin/time -p test -s "$BUILD_DIR/style.css"

/usr/bin/time -p env PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR" BUILD_DIR="$BUILD_DIR" OPENCODE_WEB_DIR="$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" node --input-type=commonjs -e '
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  const path = require("node:path");
  const project = path.resolve(process.env.PROJECT_DIR);
  const directory = path.resolve(process.env.BUILD_DIR);
  if (!directory.startsWith(project + path.sep)) throw new Error("Built directory must be inside the project.");
  fs.mkdirSync(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, "deployment-output.json"), JSON.stringify({ project, directory }, null, 2) + "\n");
'

exec /usr/bin/time -p python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory "$BUILD_DIR"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing playable game with cycling enemy lock-on, less passive/retreating boss movement, improved Vesper and Morrow visuals and animations, and a giant ice-pillar attack from the mage.

## Requirements
- Pressing Q should lock onto the next enemy instead of unlocking.
- Make bosses less likely to move backward, especially ranged bosses; have them idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and graphic.
- Add a huge attack where the mage shoots a giant ice pillar at the player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions have been made yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located the existing lock-on, duo boss AI, Vesper and Morrow models/poses, and frost attack code.

### Active
- Implement the requested gameplay and visual changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change Q from lock toggle to cycle through valid enemy targets, updating the lock-on HUD as needed.
2. Adjust duo movement to reduce retreating and favor more deliberate idle/approach behavior.
3. Improve Vesper and Morrow’s procedural models and animations.
4. Add a clearly telegraphed, large ice-pillar projectile attack for Vesper and verify gameplay behavior.
5. Sync `game.js` and related page changes to `dist/`, then run available checks or a browser play test.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Main implementation for lock-on, duo AI, models, animations, and attacks.
- `index.html`: Displays Q’s current “auto-lock nearest enemy / release” controls text.
- `dist/game.js`: Served game copy; currently identical to `game.js`.
- `dist/index.html`: Served page copy; currently identical to `index.html`.
- `start.sh`: Copies root game files into `dist/` before serving.

## Important Context
- Q currently invokes `toggleLock()`; when already locked, it releases the lock.
- `lockTargetInfo()` currently returns only the nearest valid target, including either living twin during the duo fight.
- Vesper is twin `id: 0` and uses `frostbolt`, `frostfall`, and `frostwave`; existing `frostfall` spawns several ground-targeted ice pillars, not a launched pillar projectile.
- Vesper and Morrow use procedural `buildKnight` models and custom procedural poses in `poseDuo()`.
- No files have been changed; the repository appeared clean.

## Objective
- Improve lock-on cycling, duo-boss AI and visuals, and add Vesper’s telegraphed giant ice-pillar attack.

## Requirements
- Q cycles to the next enemy instead of unlocking.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected lock-on logic, duo AI and models/poses, frost hazards, update loop, and served-file workflow.

### Active
- Add persistent lock-target selection and Q cycling; update the lock-on HUD and control text.
- Tune `updateDuoTwin()` so Vesper retreats less and both bosses move less while in range.
- Improve duo models and animations.
- Implement Vesper’s launched ice pillar attack and its collision, updates, and cleanup.
- Sync root game files to `dist/` and run available checks or a browser play test.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add persistent lock-target selection and Q cycling.
2. Tune duo movement and idle behavior.
3. Improve duo models and animations.
4. Implement Vesper’s launched ice pillar and cleanup.
5. Sync served files and run available checks or a browser play test.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Lock-on, duo AI/models/poses, attacks, hazard lifecycle, and update loop.
- `index.html`: Lock-on hint and control text.
- `dist/game.js`: Served game copy.
- `dist/index.html`: Served page copy.
- `package.json`: Test script is a placeholder; no test suite is configured.
- `start.sh`: Copies root game files into `dist/` before serving.

## Important Context
- No implementation changes have been made; the working tree is clean.
- `lockTargetInfo()` currently chooses the nearest valid target without retaining selection; `toggleLock()` unlocks on Q when already locked. `G.locked` is initialized when duo combat begins.
- Duo targets are in `duoTwins`; Vesper is `id: 0`. `updateDuoTwin()` uses desired ranges 9 and 3.5, retreats when too close, and strafes while in range.
- Vesper’s attacks are `frostbolt`, `frostfall`, and `frostwave`; `spawnHexPillar()` creates delayed ground-targeted hazards, not launched projectiles.
- Duo updates already call `updateHexBolts(dt)`, `updateHexPillars(dt)`, and `updateHexWaves(dt)`; `clearHexHazards()` runs during duo reset.
- Vesper and Morrow use `duoAK` and `duoBK`, built with `buildKnight()` and animated by `poseDuo()`.

- Complete the existing game changes: improve lock-on cycling and duo-boss behavior/visuals, and add Vesper’s telegraphed launched ice-pillar attack.

## Requirements
- Q locks the nearest enemy initially, then cycles targets instead of unlocking.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, should retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Retain the selected target’s identity and cycle through available enemies in distance order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected lock-on logic, skeleton spawning, duo AI/models/poses, frost hazards, update loop, and served-file workflow.

### Active
- Implement stable target identity and Q cycling in `lockTargetInfo()` and `toggleLock()`; update the HUD and control text.
- Tune boss movement to retreat less and idle more, especially duo/ranged behavior.
- Improve duo-specific visual and animation detail.
- Implement Vesper’s telegraphed ice-pillar projectile and cleanup.
- Sync root game files to `dist/` and run available checks or a browser play test.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add stable IDs for skeletons and stable lock-target keys for all target types; make Q acquire nearest or cycle by distance.
2. Tune movement and idle behavior for bosses, then refine duo models and poses.

- `dist/index.html`: Served page copy.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the game changes: make Q cycle lock-on targets, improve duo-boss behavior and visuals, and add Vesper’s telegraphed launched ice-pillar attack.

## Requirements
- Q locks the nearest enemy initially, then cycles targets instead of unlocking.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, should retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Retain the selected target’s identity and cycle through available enemies in distance order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial launched-pillar scaffolding in `game.js`: spawn, update, cleanup functions, and the `launchedIcePillars` collection.
- Added `G.lockTargetKey` to game state.

### Active
- Add stable target keys for bosses, duo twins, and skeletons; make Q acquire nearest or cycle by distance.
- Tune duo movement to reduce retreat and increase idle time; improve twins’ visuals and animations. Consider reducing Morgana’s retreat.
- Connect Vesper’s launched-pillar attack to attack selection, telegraph, release, update, and cleanup.
- Update control hints, sync root files to `dist/`, then run available checks or a browser play test.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement stable target keys and cycling in lock-on logic; change Q from toggle-off to cycling.
2. Tune duo movement and attack cadence; improve the twins’ visuals and animations, and consider Morgana’s retreat.
3. Add a visible aim telegraph and connect Vesper’s pillar attack to the game lifecycle.
4. Update control hints, sync `game.js` and `index.html` to `dist/`, and run available checks or a browser play test.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Lock-on logic, duo AI/models/poses, Morgana movement, and launched-pillar scaffolding.
- `index.html`: Control instructions to update.
- `dist/game.js`: Served game copy to sync.
- `dist/index.html`: Served page copy to sync.
- `package.json`: Test script is a placeholder; no test suite is configured.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; latest status showed only `game.js` modified.
- `lockTargetInfo()` currently chooses the nearest target on every call, and Q currently unlocks when already locked.
- Duo twins have numeric IDs, but skeletons do not yet have stable IDs.
- Duo movement currently targets distance 9 for Vesper and 3.5 for Morrow; both retreat when too close and strafe in range.
- Vesper’s existing attacks are `frostbolt`, `frostfall`, and `frostwave`; `spawnHexPillar()` makes delayed ground-targeted hazards.
- `spawnLaunchedIcePillar()`, `updateLaunchedIcePillars()`, and `clearLaunchedIcePillars()` exist but are not connected to attack selection or the game lifecycle; the update loop does not call `updateLaunchedIcePillars()`, and `clearHexHazards()` does not call `clearLaunchedIcePillars()`.
- `updateWitch()` retreats when the player is within 6.5 units; Morgana’s movement and attack cadence may need tuning.

## Objective
- Complete the game changes: make Q cycle lock-on targets, improve duo-boss behavior and visuals, and add Vesper’s telegraphed launched ice-pillar attack.

## Requirements
- Q locks the nearest enemy initially, then cycles targets instead of unlocking.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, should retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Retain the selected target’s identity and cycle through available enemies in distance order.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `G.lockTargetKey` and scaffolding for `launchedIcePillars`, `spawnLaunchedIcePillar()`, `updateLaunchedIcePillars()`, and `clearLaunchedIcePillars()` in `game.js`.

### Active
- Assign stable target keys to bosses, duo twins, and skeletons; make Q acquire nearest or cycle by distance.
- Tune duo movement and attack cadence to reduce retreat and increase idle time; improve twins’ visuals and animations. Consider reducing Morgana’s retreat.
- Add an aim telegraph and connect the launched pillar to Vesper’s attack selection, release, update, and cleanup.
- Update control hints, sync root files to `dist/`, then run available checks or a browser play test.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement stable target keys and cycling in lock-on logic; change Q from toggle-off to cycling.
2. Tune duo movement and attack cadence; improve the twins’ visuals and animations, and consider Morgana’s retreat.
3. Add a telegraph and connect the launched pillar throughout the game lifecycle.
4. Update control hints, sync `game.js` and `index.html` to `dist/`, then run available checks or a browser play test.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Lock-on, duo AI/models/poses, Morgana movement, skeleton spawning, and launched-pillar scaffolding.
- `index.html`: Control instructions to update.
- `dist/game.js`: Served game copy to sync.
- `dist/index.html`: Served page copy to sync.
- `package.json`: Test script is a placeholder; no test suite is configured.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `M game.js`.
- `lockTargetInfo()` currently chooses the nearest target on every call; Q currently unlocks when already locked. `G.lockTargetKey` is present but unused.
- Duo twins have numeric IDs, but skeletons do not yet have stable IDs.
- Duo movement currently targets distance 9 for Vesper and 3.5 for Morrow; both retreat when too close and strafe in range.
- Vesper’s existing attacks are `frostbolt`, `frostfall`, and `frostwave`; `spawnHexPillar()` makes delayed ground-targeted hazards.
- Launched-pillar functions are not connected to attack selection or lifecycle; the main loop does not call `updateLaunchedIcePillars()`, and `clearHexHazards()` does not call `clearLaunchedIcePillars()`.
- `updateWitch()` retreats when the player is within 6.5 units; Morgana’s movement and attack cadence may need tuning.

## Objective
- Complete Q target cycling, tune boss movement and cadence, improve Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations, and finish Vesper’s telegraphed launched ice-pillar attack.
- Sync served copies and run available checks or a browser play test.

## Requirements
- Q acquires the nearest enemy initially, then cycles targets rather than unlocking.
- Retain the selected target’s identity and cycle through available enemies in distance order.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, should retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Update control hints and served copies; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use stable keys for bosses, duo twins, and skeletons so cycling can retain the selected target.
- Keep Q cycling when locked; no Q-to-unlock behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added distance-sorted target candidates and stable keys; Q acquires the nearest target, then cycles through candidates.
- Reduced duo and witch retreat movement and adjusted attack delays to allow more idle time.
- Added Vesper’s ice-lance attack, aiming-line telegraph, projectile hit and expiry behavior, and cleanup/update integration.
- Updated Q control hints in `index.html` and `dist/index.html`.
- Added distinguishing details for Vesper (mask and candles) and Morrow (chains and bell).

### Active
- Further improve Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations in `game.js`; duo animations already run through `poseKnight()` and `poseDuo()`.
- Sync `game.js` to `dist/game.js`.
- Run syntax checks and attempt browser verification.

### Blocked
- `npm test` is a placeholder and exits with `Error: no test specified`.
- Browser verification has not been run; `playwright-cli` is available, but its setup and use remain pending.

## Next Move
1. Continue model and animation improvements in `game.js`.
2. Sync `game.js` to `dist/game.js`.
3. Run syntax checks and attempt browser verification if tooling is available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: target cycling, boss tuning, duo models and animations, ice-pillar attack.
- `dist/game.js`: served script that needs syncing.
- `index.html`: updated control hints.
- `dist/index.html`: served control hints.
- `package.json`: test script is a placeholder.
- `start.sh`: copies the main HTML, JS, and CSS into `dist/` when starting the server.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Latest observed `git status --short`: `dist/index.html`, `game.js`, and `index.html` are modified; `dist/game.js` is not.
- `game.js` contains `lockTargetCandidates()`, duo model setup near line 3325, launched-ice behavior near line 3901, duo AI near line 4903, and `poseDuo()` near line 5116.

## Objective
- Complete Q target cycling and boss-behavior tuning, improve Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations, and verify Vesper’s telegraphed launched ice-pillar attack in the served build.

## Requirements
- Q acquires the nearest enemy, then cycles through available enemies in distance order while retaining target identity.
- Bosses, especially ranged bosses, should retreat less and idle more.
- Make Vesper and Morrow’s models and animations more realistic and detailed.
- Add a telegraphed giant ice pillar launched by Vesper at the player.
- Update control hints and served copies; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use stable keys for bosses, duo twins, and skeletons so cycling retains the selected target.
- Keep Q cycling while locked; Q does not unlock.
- Vesper’s ice-lance release aims toward the player’s position at release time.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added distance-sorted target candidates and stable target identity for target cycling.
- Reduced duo and witch retreat movement and adjusted attack delays to allow more idle time.
- Added Vesper’s ice-lance attack, aiming-line telegraph, projectile hit and expiry behavior, and cleanup/update integration.
- Updated Q control hints in both HTML copies.
- Added Vesper’s mask, candelabrum, animated candle flames and lights, glowing eyes, and chest sigil; added Morrow’s chains, bell, and animated clapper.
- Synced `game.js` to `dist/game.js`; verified both scripts parse as ES modules and match.
- Captured desktop and mobile served pages; the title screen rendered without reported browser errors.

### Active
- Verify the duo encounter in-browser, including Vesper’s telegraph, launch, hit/miss behavior, and both characters’ animations.

### Blocked
- `npm test` remains a placeholder and exits with `Error: no test specified`.

## Next Move
1. Exercise the duo encounter in-browser and verify Vesper’s telegraph, launch, hit/miss behavior, and animations; prior browser captures only showed the title screen, and auto-start reported `not-found`.
2. Re-run syntax and served-copy checks after any further changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay, target cycling, boss tuning, duo models/animations, and ice-pillar attack.
- `dist/game.js`: served script; currently synced with `game.js`.
- `index.html`, `dist/index.html`: updated control hints.
- `capture-browser.mjs`: browser capture and runtime-error check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files are `game.js`, `dist/game.js`, `index.html`, and `dist/index.html`.
- A local server was started for `dist` on port `3000`; captures used `CAPTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
- `window.__game` exposes duo encounter APIs, including `enterBossArena`, `beginDuo`, `updateDuo`, and `duoTwins`, useful for driving browser verification.
